A SIDEWAYS FINDING FROM 2026-08-31 — nothing in the session was looking for it, and it turned up five times before it was noticed as a pattern.

═══ FIVE CAPABILITIES, EACH BUILT, EACH REACHABLE, EACH ALMOST UNREACHED ═══
    the `optimize` skill                 run 2 times, ever
    Constraint + budget_report           4 Constraints exist; 3 are budgets
    set_capability_signature             3 of 192 capabilities carry a signature
    Interface as a VERIFIES target       3 of 22 interfaces carry a check
    the GraphRead trait                  3 of 45 struct-coupled modules sit behind it

None of these is broken. Each was built deliberately, each works, each has a second implementation or a passing check behind it. What none of them has is REACH.

⭐⭐ AND THE THING WORTH KEEPING IS HOW ALL FIVE WERE FOUND: THE SAME QUERY SHAPE, HAND-ROLLED EVERY TIME. Each number above answers "how many of my declared X carry a Y?" — how many Interfaces have an incoming VERIFIES, how many Capabilities have an outgoing SATISFIES or a signature, how many modules sit behind a trait. Every one was computed with an ad-hoc script over the committed export, because NO SERVED TOOL ANSWERS THAT QUESTION. Verified with `find_tools` rather than assumed: querying "count edges of one type pointing at nodes of another type" returns `scan_nodes` (lists nodes, not edges) and two bulk WRITERS. The read does not exist.

═══ WHY THIS IS THE MISSING THIRD LEG, FIVE TIMES OVER ═══
`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` says vocabulary reaches a design only with a TYPED TOOL + an INSTRUCTION + A DETECTOR THAT NOTICES ABSENCE. All five above have the tool. Several have the instruction. NONE has a detector, and the reason is now concrete rather than cultural: the detector for "this vocabulary is declared and nobody uses it" would be exactly the query shape that does not exist.

⭐ IT ALSO SEPARATES TWO THINGS `dec:bl-155` SAYS IT CANNOT SEPARATE. That decision measured 40 of 132 tools never called and states outright that it CANNOT TELL UNUSED FROM UNREACHABLE. A per-type coverage query answers a different question and does not have that blind spot: `set_capability_signature` at 3 of 192 is not unreachable — it is reachable, documented, and unreached, which is a distinct diagnosis with a distinct repair.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. (1) That low reach is a DEFECT in any of the five — a capability built ahead of its need and one that failed to catch on look identical here, which is the same caution `consumption_report` states about itself. (2) That a coverage query would have CAUSED any of them to be used; it would have made the absence visible, which is necessary and not sufficient. (3) The five were not sampled systematically — they are the ones one session happened to touch in one day, so the true rate across reflow2's vocabulary is unmeasured and could be better or worse.
